ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $A(-1, 6)$ is a point on the hyperbola $y=\frac{k}{x}$ $(x<0)$. Let $P$ be a point on the positive half of the $y$-axis. Rotating point $A$ counterclockwise by $90^\circ$ around point $P$ precisely lands it on another point $B$ on the hyperbola. What are the coordinates of point $B$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw $AM \perp OM$ at point M through point A, and draw $BN \perp OM$ at point N through point B, \\
$\therefore \angle PMA = \angle BNP = 90^\circ$, \\
$\because$ Rotating point A $90^\circ$ counterclockwise around point P precisely lands on another point B on the hyperbola, \\
$\therefore PA=PB$, $\angle APB=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle APM + \angle BPN = \angle BPN + \angle PBN = 90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle APM = \angle PBN$, \\
$\therefore \triangle APM \cong \triangle BNP$ (AAS), \\
$\therefore AM=PN$, $PM=BN$, \\
$\because$ Point A $(-1,6)$ lies on the hyperbola $y=\frac{k}{x}$ ($x>0$), \\
$\therefore k = -1 \times 6 = -6$, $AM=PN=1$, \\
Let point P be $(m,0)$, then $OP=m$, \\
$\therefore PM=BN=6-m$, $ON=OP-PN=m-1$, \\
$\therefore$ The coordinates of point B are $(m-6, m-1)$, \\
$\therefore k = (m-6) \cdot (m-1) = -6$, solving for $m$ gives $m=3$ or $m=4$, \\
$\therefore$ The coordinates of point B are $\boxed{(-3, 2)}$ or $\boxed{(-2, 3)}$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: P lies on the y-axis above O, while A and B are on the same left-side branch of the hyperbola. From the text, A=(-1,6), so the hyperbola is xy=-6. Let B=(x,y) be unknown. Instead of parameterizing P, use the condition that P is the center of a 90° counterclockwise rotation from A to B. With rotation matrix R(x,y)=(-y,x), the relation is B-P=R(A-P), equivalently P=(I-R)^{-1}(B-RA). For A=(-1,6), RA=(-6,-1), so P=((x-y+5)/2,(x+y+7)/2). Because the image/text place P on the y-axis, its x-coordinate must be 0, hence x-y+5=0, or y=x+5. Now intersect this line with the hyperbola xy=-6: x(x+5)=-6, so x^2+5x+6=0, giving x=-3 or x=-2. Then y=2 or 3, respectively. Thus B=(-3,2) or B=(-2,3).

先描述图像：图中有直角坐标系，O 为原点，y 轴竖直向上，x 轴水平向右；P 位于 y 轴正半轴上；A、B 都在左侧同一支双曲线上，并且图中表示 A 绕 P 逆时针旋转 90°后到达 B。

再推理：由 A(-1,6) 在双曲线 y=k/x 上，得 k=(-1)·6=-6，所以双曲线为 xy=-6。设 B=(x,y)。用 90°逆时针旋转矩阵 R(u,v)=(-v,u)。因为 A 绕 P 逆时针旋转 90°到 B，所以 B-P=R(A-P)。等价于 B=RA+(I-R)P，从而 P=(I-R)^{-1}(B-RA)。对 A=(-1,6)，有 RA=(-6,-1)。因此 B-RA=(x+6,y+1)，计算得到 P=((x-y+5)/2,(x+y+7)/2)。图像与题意给出 P 在 y 轴上，所以 P 的横坐标为 0，即 (x-y+5)/2=0，得到 y=x+5。又 B 在双曲线 xy=-6 上，所以 x(x+5)=-6，即 x^2+5x+6=0，解得 x=-3 或 x=-2。对应 y=x+5，分别得到 y=2 或 y=3。两个点对应的 P 纵坐标分别为 3 和 4，均在 y 轴正半轴上，符合题意。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, $A(-1, 6)$ is a point on the hyperbola $y=\frac{k}{x}$ $(x<0)$. Let $P$ be a point on the positive half of the $y$-axis. Rotating point $A$ counterclockwise by $90^\circ$ around point $P$ precisely lands it on another point $B$ on the hyperbola. What are the coordinates of point $B$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw $AM \perp OM$ at point M through point A, and draw $BN \perp OM$ at point N through point B, \\
$\therefore \angle PMA = \angle BNP = 90^\circ$, \\
$\because$ Rotating point A $90^\circ$ counterclockwise around point P precisely lands on another point B on the hyperbola, \\
$\therefore PA=PB$, $\angle APB=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle APM + \angle BPN = \angle BPN + \angle PBN = 90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle APM = \angle PBN$, \\
$\therefore \triangle APM \cong \triangle BNP$ (AAS), \\
$\therefore AM=PN$, $PM=BN$, \\
$\because$ Point A $(-1,6)$ lies on the hyperbola $y=\frac{k}{x}$ ($x>0$), \\
$\therefore k = -1 \times 6 = -6$, $AM=PN=1$, \\
Let point P be $(m,0)$, then $OP=m$, \\
$\therefore PM=BN=6-m$, $ON=OP-PN=m-1$, \\
$\therefore$ The coordinates of point B are $(m-6, m-1)$, \\
$\therefore k = (m-6) \cdot (m-1) = -6$, solving for $m$ gives $m=3$ or $m=4$, \\
$\therefore$ The coordinates of point B are $\boxed{(-3, 2)}$ or $\boxed{(-2, 3)}$.

Image description: The figure has a rectangular coordinate system, with the x-axis horizontal to the right and the y-axis vertical upward. One branch of the hyperbola is drawn in the second quadrant, that is, located to the left of the y-axis and above the x-axis. Point A is at a relatively high position on this hyperbola, point B is at a relatively low position on the same branch of the hyperbola, and point P is drawn on the positive half of the y-axis. Segments PA and PB are connected, and a right-angle relationship is marked at P, matching the situation where A is rotated 90° counterclockwise about P to B.

Reasoning: From A(-1,6) being on the hyperbola y=k/x, obtain k=(-1)·6=-6, so the hyperbola satisfies xy=-6. Let P=(0,p), where p>0. Vector PA corresponds to A-P=(-1,6-p). Rotating vector (x,y) 90° counterclockwise gives (-y,x), so after rotation A-P becomes (p-6,-1). Therefore B=P+(p-6,-1)=(p-6,p-1). Because B is also on the hyperbola xy=-6, (p-6)(p-1)=-6. Expanding gives p^2-7p+6=-6, that is, p^2-7p+12=0, which factors as (p-3)(p-4)=0, so p=3 or p=4. Substitute into B=(p-6,p-1): when p=3, B=(-3,2); when p=4, B=(-2,3).
